payload.title: The replay_dev feedback source is accepted by the CLI add path, import_feedback and evidence_chain entries, so the documented guarantee that only feed_dev_misses mints it and a DEV-check case never writes one is not structural: an imported row can suppress or plant a DEV miss.
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback.py:36-38 (replay_dev is added to the one FEEDBACK_SOURCES set; the comment claims feed_dev_misses is its only minter)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback.py:157-158 (the CLI add path validates --source against the same set)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cli.py:993 (feedback add --source is a free string, default operator)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback.py:334-336 (import_feedback validates source against the same set)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback.py:360 (an imported record is copied whole, so subject_ref and defect_id survive normalization)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback.py:510-511 (every evidence_chain entry may also name replay_dev as its source_type)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/role_fitness.py:476-480 (the dedup set trusts any missed_signal row whose source is replay_dev)
docs/aria/CONTRACTS.md:1275-1276 (the contract: a replay_dev row is minted once per known miss by feed_dev_misses; a DEV-check case never produces one)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier hierarchy (make the wrong behaviour impossible, do not only document it) and docs/aria/CONTRACTS.md section 8.5 (replay_dev rows are minted only by role_fitness.feed_dev_misses).
payload.notes: FEEDBACK_SOURCES is the single validation set for the CLI add path, import_feedback and evidence_chain entries, and normalize_feedback_event copies every field of an imported record (feedback.py:360). An operator import of a missed_signal row with source replay_dev and the (subject_ref, defect_id) of a real DEV-train miss makes feed_dev_misses see that pair as already minted (role_fitness.py:476-480), so the real miss never reaches memory; the same row for a DEV-check subject puts into memory exactly the lesson the feed is designed to keep out (role_fitness.py:475). The row looks identical to a minted one, so nothing downstream can tell. It needs an operator or a deliberate process, not an ARIA cycle. Close condition: Keep replay_dev out of the operator-facing vocabulary: give feed_dev_misses its own internal source that the CLI add path, import_feedback and evidence_chain validation reject, and keep docs/aria/CONTRACTS.md and aria-kernel/tests/test_contracts_mirror_code.py mirroring both sets. A test in aria-kernel/tests/test_discovery_recall_d9.py imports and CLI-adds a replay_dev row and expects ValueError, while feed_dev_misses still mints its rows. Verified at origin/main a81bfa2d6.
